beats.text: Ancient Rome. Your new job: wash rich men's togas, by stomping on them in old urine.

scene.src: commons:Fullonica in Regio VI Ins 14 Pompeii by Geremia Discanno 1882.jpg

beats.text: You're a fuller. Every morning, you collect pots of urine from street corners.
Why urine? It's full of ammonia, which breaks down grease and dirt.

scene.src: commons:Pompeii - Fullonica of Veranius Hypsaeus 2 - MAN.jpg

beats.text: You stand in a stone tub for hours, treading the cloth like grapes.
The emperor Vespasian even taxed the urine trade.

scene.src: commons:Bust of the Emperor Vespasian (Titus Flavius Vespasianus, 9–79) MET DP157992.jpg

beats.text: When his son complained, he held up a coin and said: money doesn't smell.
Then the fumes. White wool is bleached over burning sulfur, and you breathe it all day.

scene.src: commons:Fullonica in Regio VI ins 14 Pompeii by Geremia Discanno (2) pub 1882.jpg

beats.text: And if you ruin a client's toga, you pay for it.
Would YOU survive? Type SURVIVE or DEAD.
